affectedPublicSurfaces: NO PUBLIC PRODUCT SURFACE, stated plainly rather than invented. This slice touches `agent-runtime/scripts/ci/common.py`, `agent-runtime/scripts/validate/check_module_drift.py`, `tests/harness/`, `docs/architecture/map.md` and one `MODULE.md`. Nothing it changes is imported by `backend/src/juli_backend/**`, served by any `/v1` route, bundled into `apps/**`, deployed by `release.yml`, or present in any runtime image. There is no candidate process to point a browser at, no seller-visible behaviour, and no migration. The verification for this slice is the gate's own behaviour on a real tree - that is the honest gate, and this plan uses it as one rather than dressing a harness fix in a deployment story it does not have.

The surface it DOES have is the `module_md_sync` gate result consumed by the `validate` skill and by every issue-tier PR that runs it. Today that result is a VACUOUS PASS. Measured on this branch, 2026-09-14, by importing the module directly: `parse_architecture_map()` returns 0 modules. Therefore `module_for_file` resolves nothing, `touched` in `check_module_drift.py::run_check` is always the empty set, the per-module loop never executes, and `run_check` returns `(True, 'MODULE.md in sync for touched modules', {'drift': [], 'missingInterfaces': []})` for every PR regardless of what changed.

A FIFTH DEFECT THE ISSUE DOES NOT NAME, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MAKES THE OTHERS MOOT. `parse_architecture_map` keys its dict on the module path EXACTLY as `map.md` writes it - the full `backend/src/juli_backend/services/operations` form. `module_for_file` first calls `normalize_backend_module_path`, which rewrites `backend/src/juli_backend/X` to `backend/X`, and then matches the rewritten path against those keys. Measured directly: `module_for_file('backend/src/juli_backend/services/operations/outcome_tracking.py', {'backend/src/juli_backend/services/operations': ...})` returns `None`, because `normalize_backend_module_path` turned the input into `backend/services/operations/outcome_tracking.py`. FIXING `MODULE_ROW_RE` ALONE LEAVES THE GATE EXACTLY AS VACUOUS. The two functions must be fixed as a pair and asserted as a pair.

`MODULE_ROW_RE` confirmed non-matching, with the mechanism: the pattern is ``r"\[`([^`]+)`]([^)]*MODULE\.md)?\s*\|\s*(\d+)\s*\|"`` and every real row is a markdown link, `| [`backend/src/juli_backend/services/operations`](../../backend/src/juli_backend/services/operations/MODULE.md) | 2 | ... |`. Group 2's `[^)]*` excludes only `)`, so it happily consumes the OPENING paren and the whole target up to `MODULE.md` - and then the pattern demands `\s*\|` where the next character is the link's closing `)`. Group 2 is optional, so the engine also tries skipping it, and then demands `\s*\|` immediately after the backtick-bracket where the next character is `(`. Both alternatives fail; there is no third.

`BACKTICK_SYMBOL_RE` ALREADY MANUFACTURES FALSE DOCUMENTED SYMBOLS, and widening it will manufacture more. Measured on `backend/src/juli_backend/services/operations/MODULE.md` by calling the parsers directly: 9 documented symbols, 42 code symbols, 6 orphan, 39 undocumented. The six 'orphans' are `COUNTABLE_CONFIDENCES`, `EXCLUDED_CONFIDENCES`, `missing`, `pending`, `unavailable`, `workflow_outcome_metrics` - and `pending`/`unavailable`/`missing` are the chain's link vocabulary mentioned as backticked PROSE WORDS inside a sentence, not documented symbols at all. Any bare backticked lowercase word inside a Public Interface section is read as a public symbol today.

`ast_public_symbols` MANUFACTURES FALSE UNDOCUMENTED SYMBOLS TOO, and this is what makes acceptance criterion 5 wider than it looks. Its `ast.Assign` branch admits any module-level name whose value is an `ast.Call`, so `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` is counted as a public symbol of EVERY module that has one - `logger` is in the 39 measured above. So are `main` and `build_parser` from `production_write_authorizations_cli.py`, a CLI entrypoint module. Driving `services/operations` to zero orphan AND zero undocumented therefore requires either documenting `logger` in a MODULE.md (absurd) or narrowing the CODE-side extractor - which changes the counts for every Tier 1/2 module at once, not just this one.

The numbers above were recomputed on this branch today and differ from both earlier reports (#1656's executor measured 6/33 on 2026-09-09; the issue body says 6/39). RECOMPUTE AT IMPLEMENTATION TIME and cite what you measure - do not copy any of the three figures, including these.

Merge-lane consequence, which is a real constraint on how this lands: the diff touches `agent-runtime/scripts/**`, which is CODE. This is the STANDARD lane (branch/worktree -> PR -> land on green), never the fast-track docs-only lane, and it is not the sanctioned harness-path `--admin` case either, since that case is confined to `.cursor/skills/**` / `agent-runtime/docs/**` plus the three companions the harness mandates. Turning a vacuously-green gate genuinely green is a red-until-allowlisted event for every open PR, so the allowlist must land in the SAME commit as the parser fix - never as a follow-up.

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: There is NO candidate deployment for this slice and none is needed - nothing here ships to a product app, a backend runtime, or a release workflow. The verification route is the gate's own behaviour on a real tree: pytest run from the worktree root with PYTHONPATH pinned to the worktree's backend/src, plus a direct invocation of `python agent-runtime/scripts/validate/check_module_drift.py --issue 1859` in a checkout that has a real changed-file set. Every parser assertion runs against the REAL `docs/architecture/map.md` and the REAL `backend/src/juli_backend/services/operations/MODULE.md`, not only against fixtures, because the entire defect is that the pattern and the real files disagree - a fixture written to match the pattern would pass today and prove nothing. Fixtures are used only for the cases the real tree does not currently contain (a second `##`/`###` Public Interface section, a call-signature entry, a deliberately introduced mismatch).
candidateVerificationJourney.notes: These four fields are answered honestly rather than omitted. `syntheticShopRequired` is FALSE: no shop, no tenant, no database is involved anywhere in this slice - the gate reads files and a git diff. `apiSideEffectsInScope` is FALSE: nothing is written to any table, no vendor call is made, no HTTP request is issued, and no process state changes. `workersDisabledOnCandidate` is recorded TRUE because there is no candidate process of any kind and TRUE is the safest value that cannot be misread as 'a candidate ran workers'; it is not a claim that workers were disabled on something, it is a claim that nothing ran. If a reviewer reads this section expecting a deployed candidate, the correct conclusion is that this issue has no public-release surface - see affectedPublicSurfaces - not that the journey was skipped.

journeys.name: the-gate-resolves-real-modules-and-fails-on-real-drift
assertions: `parse_architecture_map()` against the REAL `docs/architecture/map.md` returns a NONZERO module count, and the returned keys include `backend/src/juli_backend/services/operations` - the exact string that file's row carries today. Asserted against the real file, never a fixture, because the defect is precisely that the pattern and the file disagree

THE PAIRED ASSERTION, and the one the issue omits: `module_for_file('backend/src/juli_backend/services/operations/outcome_tracking.py', parse_architecture_map())` returns that module path. Asserted END-TO-END through BOTH functions on the REAL map, because each is green in isolation while the pair is broken - `normalize_backend_module_path` rewrites the input to `backend/services/...` while the map's keys are `backend/src/juli_backend/...`. A test that only checks the regex leaves the gate vacuous and claims otherwise

`check_module_drift.py::run_check` over a changed-file set containing a real Tier 1/2 backend path produces a NON-EMPTY `touched` set and therefore actually enters its per-module loop - asserted on the gate's own returned details payload, since 'returned True' is indistinguishable between the fixed and the vacuous state and is exactly what has been passing for every PR

THE ANTI-VACUUM GUARD: a test that FAILS if `parse_architecture_map()` ever returns zero modules again, pinned to the defect itself - the same shape `tests/unit/test_juli_app_grants_cover_mutations.py::test_the_scan_is_not_vacuous` uses for the AST scanner. Without it, the next edit to `MODULE_ROW_RE` or to `map.md`'s row format can silently restore the vacuum and every downstream test will still pass

drift-detected case: a deliberately introduced code/doc mismatch in a Tier 1/2 module that is NOT in the allowlist makes `run_check` return False AND names that module and that specific symbol in `details['drift']` - asserted on the symbol, not merely on the boolean, because a gate that fails without saying what drifted is not actionable

multi-section case: a fixture MODULE.md with one `##` and one nested `###` Public Interface section returns symbols from BOTH (`finditer`, not `search`). Note precisely what `PUBLIC_SECTION_RE`'s lookahead `(?=\n##\s+|\Z)` does today - it requires `##` followed by WHITESPACE, so a `###` heading does not terminate a section; the real defect is the single `search` taking only the first match, and the fix must be asserted on that, not on a mis-stated lookahead
call-signature case: an entry written as `` `name(args) -> T` `` is recognised as the symbol `name`, asserted on a fixture containing both that form and a bare identifier

THE FALSE-POSITIVE GUARD, pinned to the three real ones measured today: backticked PROSE words inside a Public Interface section - `pending`, `unavailable`, `missing` in `services/operations/MODULE.md` - are NOT promoted to documented symbols. Widening the pattern to call signatures without constraining WHERE a symbol may be read manufactures more of these, and each false 'documented' symbol becomes a false orphan that the allowlist then has to excuse forever

allowlist shape: it is EXPLICIT and enumerated per (module, symbol), never a wildcard per module and never a bare module-name skip. An allowlist entry that no longer corresponds to real drift FAILS the suite - the same anti-rot rule the grants registry enforces with `test_every_registry_entry_still_names_a_live_call_site` - so the allowlist cannot outlive the drift it excuses or quietly become the gate's new resting state

allowlist-respected case: with the allowlist in place, `run_check` against `main` as of this slice landing returns True, and returns False the moment a change introduces drift BEYOND what is allowlisted - asserted on both halves, because an allowlist that swallows new drift is just the vacuum with extra steps

`services/operations` burn-down: the gate reports ZERO orphan and ZERO undocumented for `backend/src/juli_backend/services/operations`, and that module is REMOVED from the allowlist in the same commit. Measured starting point on this branch today: 9 documented, 42 code symbols, 6 orphan, 39 undocumented - recompute, do not copy

the burn-down's scope honesty: if reaching zero requires excluding module-level `logger` (the `ast.Assign` + `ast.Call` branch of `ast_public_symbols`) or the CLI module's `main`/`build_parser`, that is a change to the CODE-side extractor affecting EVERY Tier 1/2 module at once. Say so in the PR, and report the before/after orphan and undocumented counts for at least one OTHER Tier 1/2 module - tuning the extractor until one module reads zero, without looking at what it did to the rest, is how a gate gets re-broken while going green

the harness's own suites pass untouched: `tests/harness/test_meta_validate_e2e_public_release.py` and the full `agent-runtime/scripts/validate/` gate set. `common.py` is shared by many gates, so `MODULE_ROW_RE`, `PUBLIC_SECTION_RE`, `BACKTICK_SYMBOL_RE`, `normalize_backend_module_path` and `ast_public_symbols` each need their other consumers checked before being changed

the `ChangedFilesUnresolved` branch still fails CLOSED with its cause reported (`check_module_drift.py::run_check`) - an unresolvable diff must never become a silent pass, which is the same class of defect this slice is fixing and would be a cruel one to reintroduce while fixing it

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. The `module_md_sync` gate continues to pass vacuously for every PR - `parse_architecture_map()` keeps returning zero modules, `touched` stays empty, and the gate keeps reporting 'MODULE.md in sync for touched modules' regardless of what changed. Nothing is partially applied and no runtime is affected. But holding is NOT neutral and the PR must say so: every PR that merges while the gate is vacuous carries unverified MODULE.md drift, and the pre-existing drift in `services/operations` (6 orphan / 39 undocumented as measured today) keeps growing invisibly, exactly as it has since the gate was written.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Revert the commit. Code-only and harness-only: no deploy to reverse, no process to restart, no schema state, no data effect, no vendor effect. The gate returns to its vacuous pass and every open PR goes green again. THE HONEST CAVEAT, and it belongs in the PR and in the release metadata: a revert does not un-verify what was verified. PRs that merged green while the fix was live had their touched modules genuinely checked; PRs that merge after a revert did not, and nothing in the repository marks which is which. A second honest caveat: if `services/operations/MODULE.md` (or the code it documents) was edited to burn down the allowlist, a revert of the SCRIPTS alone leaves those edits in place - decide deliberately whether to revert them too rather than letting a partial revert look like a clean one.

doNotInfer: Do NOT invent a public surface for this issue. It has none: no route, no app, no runtime import, no release workflow, no migration. Say that plainly in the implementation artifact. Dressing a harness fix in a deployment story it does not have is its own form of dishonest evidence.

Do NOT fix `MODULE_ROW_RE` alone and call the gate fixed. `module_for_file` normalizes `backend/src/juli_backend/X` to `backend/X` while the map's keys are the full path - the pair is what is broken. Assert end-to-end through both functions on the REAL map, or the gate stays vacuous behind a green test.

Do NOT assert the parser against a fixture `map.md` only. The entire defect is that the pattern and the REAL file disagree; a fixture written to match the pattern passes today. Fixtures are for the cases the real tree lacks (multi-section, call-signature, deliberate drift) and for nothing else.

Do NOT ship without an anti-vacuum guard. A test that fails if `parse_architecture_map()` ever returns zero again is the only thing standing between the next regex edit and a silent return to the status quo. `test_the_scan_is_not_vacuous` in `tests/unit/test_juli_app_grants_cover_mutations.py` is the shape to copy.

Do NOT widen `BACKTICK_SYMBOL_RE` without a false-positive guard. Bare backticked prose words inside a Public Interface section are already being read as symbols - `pending`, `unavailable` and `missing` in `services/operations/MODULE.md` are three real ones today. Each false 'documented' symbol becomes a false orphan the allowlist has to excuse forever.

Do NOT mis-state `PUBLIC_SECTION_RE`'s lookahead. `(?=\n##\s+|\Z)` requires `##` followed by whitespace, so a `###` sub-heading does NOT terminate a section. The real defect is the single `search` taking only the first match. Fix what is actually broken.

Do NOT make the allowlist a wildcard, a per-module skip, or a permanent fixture. It is explicit per (module, symbol), it fails the suite when an entry no longer names real drift, and it is temporary by design. An allowlist that cannot rot is the difference between a gate with a known debt and a gate that is off.
Do NOT land the allowlist in a follow-up. Turning a vacuously-green gate genuinely green goes red for every open PR on day one; the allowlist ships in the SAME commit as the parser fix.

Do NOT tune `ast_public_symbols` until one module reads zero without looking at the rest. Excluding module-level `logger` or a CLI module's `main`/`build_parser` changes the counts for EVERY Tier 1/2 module. Report the before/after for at least one other module, and say in the PR that the extractor changed.

Do NOT delete or weaken the `ChangedFilesUnresolved` branch. An unresolvable diff must keep failing CLOSED with its cause reported (#1540, #1571) - reintroducing a silent pass while fixing a silent pass would be the whole point missed.

Do NOT change `common.py`'s shared helpers without checking their other consumers. `normalize_backend_module_path`, `backend_module_root`, `ast_public_symbols`, `criterion_matches_test` and the ADR/handoff patterns are used by other gates in `agent-runtime/scripts/validate/`; a change that fixes this gate and breaks another is a net loss.

Do NOT treat this as a docs-only change. `agent-runtime/scripts/**` is code: STANDARD lane, PR, land on green. It is not fast-track and it is not the sanctioned harness-path `--admin` case, which is confined to `.cursor/skills/**` / `agent-runtime/docs/**` plus the three companions the harness mandates.

Do NOT rewrite `docs/architecture/map.md`'s rows wholesale as a shortcut. If the row format is normalised instead of the regex widened, that is a legitimate choice - but pick ONE, say why in the PR, and do not change the semantic content of any row while doing it. `map.md` is the Tier-2 as-built registry and `tests/unit/test_code_standard_exemplars.py` fails CI when a path a pointer document names stops existing.
Do NOT touch apps/**, packages/**, ios/** - this epic's doNotLoad list - and do not open the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051).
